COMP 4531 - Final Project¶

Automated Classification of Steel Surface Defects Using CNNs¶

Author: Michael Ghattas
Quarter: Q4 2025

1. Problem Statement and Project Goals¶

In high-volume manufacturing (e.g., aerospace and steel production), surface quality inspection is critical for safety and cost. Manual visual inspection is inconsistent, slow, and error-prone.
This project uses deep learning to automatically classify steel surface defects from images.

Goal:
Given a grayscale image of a steel surface, predict one of six defect classes from the NEU-DET dataset:

  • crazing
  • inclusion
  • patches
  • pitted_surface
  • rolled-in_scale
  • scratches

We will:

  1. Explore and clean the data and justify why deep learning is appropriate.
  2. Build baseline models (logistic regression, MLP) on flattened pixels.
  3. Implement a custom CNN from scratch and analyze under/overfitting.
  4. Refine the model using regularization and data augmentation.
  5. Implement transfer learning (EfficientNetB0) and compare performance.
  6. Analyze errors and discuss limitations and future work.

# Exploratory data analysis - class distribution
def count_labels(ds) -> np.ndarray:
    counts = np.zeros(len(class_names), dtype=int)
    for _, labels in ds:
        idx = np.argmax(labels.numpy(), axis=1)
        for i in idx:
            counts[i] += 1
    return counts

# Convert a tf.data.Dataset to NumPy arrays (for sklearn baselines)

def dataset_to_numpy(ds: tf.data.Dataset) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    images = []
    labels = []
    for batch_imgs, batch_labels in ds:
        images.append(batch_imgs.numpy())
        labels.append(batch_labels.numpy())
    images = np.concatenate(images, axis=0)
    labels = np.concatenate(labels, axis=0)
    return images, labels

X_train_np, y_train_np = dataset_to_numpy(train_ds_raw)
X_val_np,   y_val_np   = dataset_to_numpy(val_ds_raw)
X_test_np,  y_test_np  = dataset_to_numpy(test_ds_raw)

print("Train np:", X_train_np.shape, y_train_np.shape)
print("Val np:  ", X_val_np.shape,   y_val_np.shape)
print("Test np: ", X_test_np.shape,  y_test_np.shape)

# Flatten for sklearn baselines
X_train_flat = X_train_np.reshape(len(X_train_np), -1)
X_val_flat   = X_val_np.reshape(len(X_val_np),   -1)
X_test_flat  = X_test_np.reshape(len(X_test_np), -1)

# Helper function - plot training history
def plot_history(hist):
    acc = hist.history.get("accuracy", [])
    val_acc = hist.history.get("val_accuracy", [])
    loss = hist.history.get("loss", [])
    val_loss = hist.history.get("val_loss", [])
    epochs = range(1, len(acc) + 1)

    plt.figure(figsize=(12, 5))

    plt.subplot(1, 2, 1)
    plt.plot(epochs, acc, label="Train acc")
    plt.plot(epochs, val_acc, label="Val acc")
    plt.xlabel("Epoch")
    plt.ylabel("Accuracy")
    plt.legend()

    plt.subplot(1, 2, 2)
    plt.plot(epochs, loss, label="Train loss")
    plt.plot(epochs, val_loss, label="Val loss")
    plt.xlabel("Epoch")
    plt.ylabel("Loss")
    plt.legend()

    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

# Custom CNN v1 - baseline convolutional model
def build_cnn_model_v1(
    input_shape=(IMG_HEIGHT, IMG_WIDTH, 3),
    num_classes=NUM_CLASSES
):
    inputs = keras.Input(shape=input_shape)
    x = layers.Rescaling(1.0 / 255)(inputs)

    x = layers.Conv2D(32, 3, padding="same", activation="relu")(x)
    x = layers.MaxPooling2D(2)(x)

    x = layers.Conv2D(64, 3, padding="same", activation="relu")(x)
    x = layers.MaxPooling2D(2)(x)

    x = layers.Conv2D(128, 3, padding="same", activation="relu")(x)
    x = layers.MaxPooling2D(2)(x)

    x = layers.Flatten()(x)
    x = layers.Dense(128, activation="relu")(x)
    outputs = layers.Dense(num_classes, activation="softmax")(x)

    return keras.Model(inputs, outputs, name="cnn_v1")

cnn_v1 = build_cnn_model_v1()
cnn_v1.summary()

# Train CNN v1
cnn_v1.compile(
    optimizer=keras.optimizers.Adam(learning_rate=1e-3),
    loss="categorical_crossentropy",
    metrics=["accuracy"],
)

early_stopping_v1 = keras.callbacks.EarlyStopping(
    monitor="val_loss",
    patience=5,
    restore_best_weights=True,
)

history_v1 = cnn_v1.fit(
    train_ds,
    validation_data=val_ds,
    epochs=30,
    callbacks=[early_stopping_v1],
    verbose=1,
)

plot_history(history_v1)

def get_predictions_and_labels(ds, model):
    y_true = []
    y_pred = []
    for batch_imgs, batch_labels in ds:
        preds = model.predict(batch_imgs, verbose=0)
        y_true.append(np.argmax(batch_labels.numpy(), axis=1))
        y_pred.append(np.argmax(preds, axis=1))
    return np.concatenate(y_true), np.concatenate(y_pred)

y_true_v1, y_pred_v1 = get_predictions_and_labels(test_ds, cnn_v1)

print("\nClassification report - CNN v1:\n")
print(classification_report(y_true_v1, y_pred_v1, target_names=class_names))

cm_v1 = confusion_matrix(y_true_v1, y_pred_v1)
print("Confusion matrix - CNN v1:\n", cm_v1)

# Helper - confusion matrix plotting
import itertools

def plot_confusion_matrix(cm, classes, normalize=False, title="Confusion matrix"):
    if normalize:
        cm = cm.astype("float") / cm.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)

    plt.figure(figsize=(7, 6))
    plt.imshow(cm, interpolation="nearest", cmap="Blues")
    plt.title(title)
    plt.colorbar()
    tick_marks = np.arange(len(classes))
    plt.xticks(tick_marks, classes, rotation=45, ha="right")
    plt.yticks(tick_marks, classes)

    fmt = ".2f" if normalize else "d"
    thresh = cm.max() / 2.0
    for i, j in itertools.product(range(cm.shape[0]), range(cm.shape[1])):
        plt.text(
            j, i, format(cm[i, j], fmt),
            horizontalalignment="center",
            color="white" if cm[i, j] > thresh else "black",
        )

    plt.ylabel("True label")
    plt.xlabel("Predicted label")
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

plot_confusion_matrix(cm_v1, class_names, normalize=False, title="CNN v1 - Confusion Matrix (Counts)")
plot_confusion_matrix(cm_v1, class_names, normalize=True,  title="CNN v1 - Confusion Matrix (Normalized)")

# Custom CNN v2 - with data augmentation, BatchNorm, and L2
def build_cnn_model_v2(
    input_shape=(IMG_HEIGHT, IMG_WIDTH, 3),
    num_classes=NUM_CLASSES,
    l2_reg=1e-4
):
    inputs = keras.Input(shape=input_shape)

    x = data_augmentation(inputs)
    x = layers.Rescaling(1.0 / 255)(x)

    x = layers.Conv2D(32, 3, padding="same", activation="relu",
                      kernel_regularizer=regularizers.l2(l2_reg))(x)
    x = layers.BatchNormalization()(x)
    x = layers.MaxPooling2D(2)(x)
    x = layers.Dropout(0.2)(x)

    x = layers.Conv2D(64, 3, padding="same", activation="relu",
                      kernel_regularizer=regularizers.l2(l2_reg))(x)
    x = layers.BatchNormalization()(x)
    x = layers.MaxPooling2D(2)(x)
    x = layers.Dropout(0.3)(x)

    x = layers.Conv2D(128, 3, padding="same", activation="relu",
                      kernel_regularizer=regularizers.l2(l2_reg))(x)
    x = layers.BatchNormalization()(x)
    x = layers.MaxPooling2D(2)(x)
    x = layers.Dropout(0.4)(x)

    x = layers.Flatten()(x)
    x = layers.Dense(128, activation="relu",
                     kernel_regularizer=regularizers.l2(l2_reg))(x)
    x = layers.Dropout(0.4)(x)
    outputs = layers.Dense(num_classes, activation="softmax")(x)

    return keras.Model(inputs, outputs, name="cnn_v2")

cnn_v2 = build_cnn_model_v2()
cnn_v2.summary()

# Transfer learning - EfficientNetB0 feature extractor
from tensorflow.keras.applications import EfficientNetB0
from tensorflow.keras.applications.efficientnet import preprocess_input

def build_transfer_model(
    input_shape=(IMG_HEIGHT, IMG_WIDTH, 3),
    num_classes=NUM_CLASSES,
    dropout_rate=0.4
):
    base_model = EfficientNetB0(
        include_top=False,
        weights="imagenet",
        input_shape=input_shape,
    )
    base_model.trainable = False  # feature extractor

    inputs = keras.Input(shape=input_shape)
    x = data_augmentation(inputs)
    x = preprocess_input(x)
    x = base_model(x, training=False)
    x = layers.GlobalAveragePooling2D()(x)
    x = layers.Dropout(dropout_rate)(x)
    outputs = layers.Dense(num_classes, activation="softmax")(x)

    model = keras.Model(inputs, outputs, name="efficientnet_b0_transfer")
    return model

transfer_model = build_transfer_model()
transfer_model.summary()

print(f"Transfer model - Test loss: {test_loss_tl:.4f}")
print(f"Transfer model - Test accuracy: {test_acc_tl:.4f}")

y_true_tl, y_pred_tl = get_predictions_and_labels(test_ds, transfer_model)

print("\nClassification report - Transfer model:\n")

cm_tl = confusion_matrix(y_true_tl, y_pred_tl)

plot_confusion_matrix(cm_tl, class_names, normalize=False, title="Transfer - Confusion Matrix (Counts)")
plot_confusion_matrix(cm_tl, class_names, normalize=True,  title="Transfer - Confusion Matrix (Normalized)")

# Error analysis - visualize misclassified examples (transfer model)

# Convert test dataset to NumPy for visualization
X_test_vis, y_test_vis = X_test_np, y_test_np
y_true_vis = np.argmax(y_test_vis, axis=1)

preds_vis = transfer_model.predict(X_test_vis, verbose=0)
y_pred_vis = np.argmax(preds_vis, axis=1)

mis_idx = np.where(y_true_vis != y_pred_vis)[0]
print("Total misclassified examples:", len(mis_idx))

num_to_show = min(12, len(mis_idx))
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 12))
for i in range(num_to_show):
    idx = mis_idx[i]
    ax = plt.subplot(3, 4, i + 1)
    plt.imshow(X_test_vis[idx].astype("uint8"), cmap="gray")
    plt.title(f"True: {class_names[y_true_vis[idx]]}\nPred: {class_names[y_pred_vis[idx]]}")
    plt.axis("off")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Total misclassified examples: 62

Conclusion¶

This project applied deep learning methods to the classification of steel surface defects using the NEU-DET dataset. Starting from simple baselines (logistic regression, MLP), I demonstrated that classical models on flattened pixels perform poorly due to the complex, texture-based nature of surface defects. Custom CNNs substantially improved performance by learning spatial features, and the regularized CNN v2 introduced data augmentation and regularization techniques to better manage overfitting.
